london.name: London
london.stay: Southwark or Bloomsbury. Both put you inside walking distance of most of this list.
london.intro: Two days is a taster, not a visit. One great museum, one fortress, one market, and the river at dusk. Trying for more just means seeing less of each.

lisbon.name: Lisbon
lisbon.stay: Alfama for atmosphere, Chiado for convenience, Príncipe Real for the best food radius.
lisbon.intro: Four days, one of which belongs to Sintra. Lisbon rewards walking uphill without a plan far more than it rewards ticking off interiors.

sintra.name: Sintra
sintra.stay: Day trip from Lisbon. Train from Rossio, 40 minutes, then bus 434 or a rideshare up the hill.
sintra.intro: The single highest-impact day in Portugal. Two sites done well, or three in a rush. Never four.

porto.name: Porto
porto.stay: Ribeira for the view, Cedofeita or Baixa for the food, Gaia if you want the postcard from your window.
porto.intro: Denser, steeper and more walkable than Lisbon. Two days covers the city properly — but it costs you the Douro, which is the trip's biggest single omission.

brussels.name: Brussels
brussels.stay: Sainte-Catherine or the centre around Grand Place. Both put you inside walking distance of everything except the Atomium.
brussels.intro: Three days: one for the medieval centre, one for Art Nouveau and the museums, one for Ghent — which quietly outclasses Bruges and is half the travel time. Brussels itself rewards a slow pace far more than a checklist.

bruges.name: Bruges
bruges.stay: Don't. Sleep in Brussels and come for the day.
bruges.intro: One hour by train from Brussels, and a day trip rather than a base — staying here puts you an hour further from everything else. Go early; by eleven the coach parties own the Markt.

amsterdam.name: Amsterdam
amsterdam.stay: Jordaan or De Pijp. Avoid anything that advertises itself as being in the Red Light District.
amsterdam.intro: Three days is exactly right and a fourth would be wasted. Rent a bike on the first afternoon and stop using trams entirely.

berlin.name: Berlin
berlin.stay: Mitte for walkability, Kreuzberg or Neukölln for everything that happens after dark.
berlin.intro: The largest and most spread-out city on the trip. Three days means Wall history, museums and one proper night out. Two days means choosing between them.

munich.name: Munich
munich.stay: Ludwigsvorstadt for walking distance to the Theresienwiese, Altstadt for everything else. Book absurdly early — Oktoberfest doubles or triples room rates.
munich.intro: You arrive during Oktoberfest, which means Munich is not really Munich — it's 6 million people in a field. Give the Wiesn one full day, and use the other to see the city that exists underneath it.

ring.name: Nürburgring
ring.stay: Adenau or Nürburg itself. The Dorint sits on the GP circuit; guesthouses in Adenau are cheaper and five minutes from the Nordschleife entrance.
ring.intro: Nürburg, in the Eifel hills — 1h15 from Cologne, 2h30 from Brussels, and nowhere near Nuremberg. Green Hell Driving Days run 2–4 October: three consecutive all-day public sessions rather than the usual weekday evening slots.

egypt.name: Cairo & Giza
egypt.stay: Giza for pyramid views and festival proximity, Zamalek for a calmer island base with the best restaurants.
egypt.intro: Four days built around Starlight at the pyramids. Two festival nights, two days of Cairo — which is comfortably enough for the Giza plateau, the new museum and Islamic Cairo, and nothing like enough for Luxor.

activities.title: The British Museum
activities.description: Eight million objects under Foster's glass lattice, and free since 1759. Do not attempt the whole thing — go to Room 4 for the Rosetta Stone, Room 18 for the Parthenon marbles, Room 10 for the Assyrian lion hunt, then leave while you still like it.

activities.title: Westminster & Whitehall
activities.description: Parliament, Big Ben, the Abbey from outside, Horse Guards, Downing Street, then into St James's Park. Entirely free and the densest square mile of the London in your head.

activities.title: Tower of London
activities.description: A Norman keep that has been a palace, a prison and a mint. The Yeoman Warder tour is included and genuinely worth queuing for. Walk Tower Bridge after and look back.

activities.title: Borough Market
activities.description: The best single food stop in the city. Before noon on a Friday or you'll shuffle. Kappacasein toastie, Bread Ahead doughnut, Padella next door if the queue is human.

activities.title: Tate Modern & the South Bank
activities.description: Walk Westminster Bridge to Tower Bridge along the water — National Theatre, the Globe, Borough — and step into the Turbine Hall on the way. Free, and the city at its best.

activities.title: Thames at dusk
activities.description: Same walk, different hour. Cross Waterloo Bridge at sunset for the only view that takes in both the City and Westminster at once.

activities.title: National Gallery
activities.description: Van Eyck's Arnolfini Portrait, Turner, Caravaggio, the Wilton Diptych. Free, central, and far quicker to digest than the British Museum.

activities.title: St Paul's Cathedral
activities.description: 528 steps through the Whispering Gallery to the Golden Gallery and the best rooftop in the City.

activities.title: Covent Garden & Seven Dials
activities.description: Skip the piazza buskers and go straight to Seven Dials and Neal's Yard behind it. Neal's Yard Dairy for cheese, Monmouth for coffee.

activities.title: Soho after dark
activities.description: Old Compton Street, Bar Termini, Kiln or Bao for dinner, then a basement somewhere. London's most concentrated evening.

activities.title: Shoreditch & Brick Lane
activities.description: Street art, vintage, curry houses and the Sunday markets. East London's version of an evening.

activities.title: Notting Hill & Portobello
activities.description: Pastel terraces. The antiques market only truly runs Saturday — otherwise it's just a nice walk.

activities.title: Greenwich & Royal Observatory
activities.description: Prime meridian, Cutty Sark, the view back over Canary Wharf. Best reached by river boat.

activities.title: Camden Market
activities.description: Punk-era relic turned food court. Fun, chaotic, a museum of itself.

activities.title: Hyde Park & Kensington Gardens
activities.description: The Serpentine, Kensington Palace gardens, Speakers' Corner on Sunday.

activities.title: A West End show
activities.description: Same-day tickets from the TKTS booth in Leicester Square usually beat the box office.

activities.title: Alfama, on foot, with no plan
activities.description: The Moorish quarter that survived the 1755 earthquake because it sat on solid rock. Laundry lines, tiled façades, staircases that go nowhere. Enter at Portas do Sol and walk downhill until you are lost — this is the thing you cannot get anywhere else on the trip.
activities.details: Free · give it half a day

activities.title: Jerónimos Monastery
activities.description: Manueline architecture at its absolute limit — carved rope, coral and armillary spheres, paid for with pepper money. The cloister is the masterpiece.

activities.title: Belém Tower
activities.description: The little river fort that every Portugal photograph eventually becomes. The interior is cramped and the queue is long; the exterior may well be enough.

activities.title: Pastéis de Belém
activities.description: The original 1837 recipe, still mixed behind a locked door by a handful of people. Queue inside rather than at the takeaway window — it moves faster and they arrive warm.

activities.title: São Jorge Castle
activities.description: A fairly ordinary castle standing on the best platform in the city. Come for the terrace, the cannons and the peacocks.

activities.title: Fado in a small room
activities.description: Not a dinner show. Mesa de Frades is a converted chapel with thirty seats; A Baiuca makes the diners fall silent; Tasca do Chico is the rowdy one. Book before you fly.

activities.title: Praça do Comércio & Baixa
activities.description: The grid Pombal threw up after the earthquake, opening straight onto the Tagus. Climb the Rua Augusta arch for the view back up the hill.

activities.title: The miradouro circuit
activities.description: Portas do Sol, Santa Luzia, Graça, Senhora do Monte, Santa Catarina. Lisbon is a city of viewpoints — treat this as an attraction, not as filler between them.

activities.title: Carmo Convent
activities.description: A Gothic church left roofless since 1755 as a deliberate memorial, sky where the ceiling was. Quietly the most affecting place in central Lisbon.

activities.title: Gulbenkian Museum
activities.description: One oil magnate's private collection — Egyptian, Islamic, Rembrandt, an entire room of Lalique — inside a modernist garden. The most underrated museum in Portugal.

activities.title: National Tile Museum
activities.description: Five centuries of azulejo in a former convent, including a 23-metre panorama of Lisbon before the earthquake. Explains a visual language you'll keep seeing all the way to Amsterdam.

activities.title: Time Out Market
activities.description: Touristy and still the best single survey of Portuguese cooking in one room. Go at 12:00 or 18:00, never 20:00.

activities.title: LX Factory
activities.description: A print works under the bridge turned bookshop, rooftop and Sunday market. Good half-afternoon, better on a Sunday.

activities.title: Padrão dos Descobrimentos
activities.description: The Discoveries monument on the Belém waterfront, with a lift to the top and a compass rose laid into the plaza below.

activities.title: Cais do Sodré & Pink Street
activities.description: The nightlife strip. Pensão Amor, a former brothel turned bar, is the one worth walking into.

activities.title: Príncipe Real
activities.description: Concept shops, a botanic garden and the most grown-up drinking in the city.

activities.title: Tram 28
activities.description: The famous route, and the most pickpocketed vehicle in Portugal. Standing room from 09:00. Ride it at 08:00 from Martim Moniz or walk the same streets.

activities.title: Santa Justa Lift
activities.description: A 45-minute queue for a view you get free by walking up to Carmo and stepping onto the same platform from behind.

activities.title: Oceanário & Parque das Nações
activities.description: A genuinely good aquarium in a district that feels like a different city. 25 minutes out.

activities.title: Pena Palace & Park
activities.description: A Romanticist fantasy in yellow, red and tile, thrown up on a volcanic peak by a king with too much imagination. The interior is small; the terraces, the Triton gate and the 200-hectare park are the real event. Take the 09:30 slot and be inside before the coaches.

activities.title: Quinta da Regaleira
activities.description: A Gothic mansion whose garden hides an Initiation Well spiralling nine storeys into the hillside, connected by unlit tunnels to a grotto. More fun than Pena and consistently underrated.

activities.title: Castle of the Moors
activities.description: Tenth-century ramparts running along the ridge like a spine. Walk the walls — and it's the best place from which to photograph Pena.

activities.title: Monserrate Palace
activities.description: Moorish-Gothic-Mughal fusion with the finest gardens in Sintra and a fraction of the crowds. The connoisseur's choice if you've been before.

activities.title: Sintra National Palace
activities.description: The twin conical chimneys in the middle of town. Worth an hour if you're waiting for a train.

activities.title: Cabo da Roca & Cascais
activities.description: The westernmost point of continental Europe, then a seaside town for dinner. Needs a car.

activities.title: Ribeira & the Dom Luís I Bridge
activities.description: Walk the upper deck at sunset toward Gaia and the whole city arranges itself beneath you — tiled façades stacked up the gorge, rabelo boats on the water, the port lodges lighting up opposite. Eiffel's partner built the span. This is the moment Porto is for.

activities.title: São Bento Station
activities.description: Twenty thousand azulejos covering the concourse of a working railway station. Five minutes, free, and one of the great rooms in Europe.

activities.title: A port lodge in Gaia
activities.description: Taylor's for the gardens and a self-guided pace, Graham's for the best tasting, Sandeman for the theatre. Pick one — the second lodge adds almost nothing.

activities.title: Livraria Lello
activities.description: The 1906 bookshop with the crimson staircase and the stained-glass ceiling. Genuinely beautiful and genuinely crushed. First slot of the day or don't bother.

activities.title: Clérigos Tower
activities.description: 240 steps to the best 360° in the city. Timed ticket, late afternoon.

activities.title: Matosinhos seafood lunch
activities.description: Charcoal grills smoking on the pavement of Rua Heróis de França, 20 minutes on the metro. The best meal in Porto and it isn't close.

activities.title: Capela das Almas
activities.description: An entire church exterior tiled in blue and white — 16,000 azulejos on a busy shopping street. Free, and it stops you mid-stride.

activities.title: Palácio da Bolsa
activities.description: The old stock exchange, built to impress European investors. The Arabian Room is magnificently excessive. Guided tour only.

activities.title: Mercado do Bolhão
activities.description: Restored in 2022 and still a working market rather than a food court. Mornings.

activities.title: Douro Valley
activities.description: Terraced vineyards cut into schist above the river, and late September is harvest. It needs a full day and it is the first thing to add if you find a fifteenth.

activities.title: Foz do Douro
activities.description: Where the river hits the Atlantic. Tram 1 along the water is the good way to get there, and the sunset is the point.

activities.title: Six Bridges cruise
activities.description: Fifty minutes on the water in a converted rabelo. Cheap, pleasant, mildly touristy, no harm done.

activities.title: Serralves
activities.description: Contemporary art museum, a pink Art Deco villa and a large park. Half a day.

activities.title: Jardim do Morro
activities.description: The lawn at the Gaia end of the bridge. Everyone with a bottle of wine at sunset. Free.

activities.title: Grand Place, lit up at night
activities.description: Guild houses in gold leaf packed onto a single medieval square, floodlit after dark and, every other August, carpeted in a flower tapestry of half a million begonias. Hugo reportedly called it the most beautiful square in Europe; five minutes standing in the middle at 22:00 makes the case better than he could.

activities.title: Manneken Pis
activities.description: A 61cm bronze fountain of a small boy, dressed in one of the roughly a thousand costumes in his own wardrobe on rotation, and the most disproportionately famous thing in Belgium. Five minutes, mostly for the collective disbelief of the crowd around it.

activities.title: Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert
activities.description: Europe's first covered shopping arcade, glazed in 1847, still lined with chocolatiers and a cinema. Walk it slowly — this is what a 19th-century vision of luxury retail looked like.

activities.title: Cathedral of St Michael and St Gudula
activities.description: Gothic twin towers, a nave of pale stone, and stained glass that turns the whole aisle blue and gold at midday. Belgium's royal weddings and state funerals happen here.

activities.title: Mont des Arts
activities.description: The formal garden staircase between the lower and upper town, framing the single best skyline shot of the spires below. Free, five minutes, and best near sunset.

activities.title: Magritte Museum
activities.description: The largest Magritte collection anywhere — 250 works across three floors of a neoclassical mansion on Place Royale, arranged in reverse chronology so you meet the bowler hats and green apples before you see where they came from.

activities.title: Belgian waffles, fries and chocolate
activities.description: Liège waffles (dense, caramelised, eaten plain off the street) versus Brussels waffles (light, crisp, piled with toppings) is a real and ongoing argument. Fries from a proper friterie — Maison Antoine or Frit Flagey — cooked twice in beef fat, and chocolate from Pierre Marcolini or Neuhaus rather than the tourist-strip shops on Rue au Beurre.

activities.title: Grand Sablon
activities.description: Brussels' most refined district — antiques, galleries, Wittamer and Pierre Marcolini both within a block, and a weekend antiques market on the square itself that happens to fall on both your Brussels days.

activities.title: Ghent, day trip
activities.description: Thirty-three minutes by direct IC train and a fraction of the crowds Bruges pulls for the same medieval Flemish atmosphere. Gravensteen castle, the Graslei waterfront guild houses, and Van Eyck's Ghent Altarpiece inside St Bavo's Cathedral. A real university city rather than a preserved film set, and the illuminated old town after dark has won lighting awards.
activities.details: Half day, easily a full one

activities.title: Atomium & Mini-Europe
activities.description: Nine steel spheres built for the 1958 World's Fair, now a permanent oddity on the skyline with a panoramic lift and a 1950s-design exhibition inside. Mini-Europe next door is a 1:25 scale park of EU landmarks — skip it unless travelling with kids, but the Atomium itself earns the metro ride out to Heysel.

activities.title: Belgian Comic Strip Center
activities.description: A Victor Horta Art Nouveau department store turned museum of Tintin, the Smurfs and the ninety years of European comics they came from. The building is worth it even if the medium isn't your thing.

activities.title: Parc du Cinquantenaire
activities.description: A triumphal arch that borrows shamelessly from Paris, flanked by two enormous museum wings — Autoworld's vintage car collection and the Royal Museum of the Armed Forces. The park itself is the best green space in the city.

activities.title: BELvue Museum & Coudenberg
activities.description: Belgium's history since 1830 told in seven themes, with a combined ticket down into the excavated ruins of the medieval Coudenberg Palace beneath the square outside. More context on the country than anywhere else in an hour.

activities.title: Horta Museum
activities.description: Victor Horta's own house and studio in Saint-Gilles, the building that effectively launched Art Nouveau. Small, precise, and completely unlike the tourist centre.

activities.title: Marolles flea market
activities.description: Jeu de Balle square fills with a genuine junk-and-antiques flea market every morning, best and biggest on Sunday — which happens to be your last Brussels morning.

activities.title: Belgian Beer World
activities.description: A new multi-floor tasting hall on Grand Place itself, covering the country's brewing traditions with a rooftop bar looking straight down onto the square.

activities.title: Parlamentarium & the EU quarter
activities.description: A free, well-built museum inside the European Parliament explaining what the EU actually does, plus the free House of European History nearby. An odd, worthwhile hour if the politics interest you at all.

activities.title: Bruges, day trip
activities.description: The famous one — canals, the Belfry, lace and chocolate on every corner. Gets crowded fast and is further than Ghent (roughly 1hr by train); go early or pick Ghent instead. Doing both in one day is possible but rushed — you'll get the postcard version of each rather than either properly.

activities.title: The Rozenhoedkaai and the canals
activities.description: The single most photographed view in Belgium: stepped gables leaning over green water with the Belfry behind them. Bruges silted up in the 1500s and simply stopped, which is why a whole medieval trading city is still standing. Walk the Dijver and Groenerei early, before the boats start.

activities.title: Belfry of Bruges
activities.description: 366 steps up a leaning 13th-century tower for the best view in Flanders. Timed tickets in high season and a genuine queue — book it or arrive at opening.

activities.title: A canal boat
activities.description: Thirty minutes, five landing stages, no booking. Touristy and completely worth it — the city was built to be seen from the water.

activities.title: Basilica of the Holy Blood
activities.description: A Romanesque lower chapel and a violently decorated Gothic upper one, holding a relic said to be Christ's blood. Small, strange, free to enter.

activities.title: Groeningemuseum
activities.description: Flemish Primitives — Van Eyck's Madonna with Canon van der Paele, Memling, Bosch. Six centuries in a building you can cross in an hour.

activities.title: Begijnhof Ten Wijngaerde
activities.description: White houses round a courtyard of daffodils, still a Benedictine convent. Silence is enforced and it works.

activities.title: Minnewater
activities.description: The 'lake of love' at the southern edge, with swans. Five minutes from the Begijnhof and a good way to end.

activities.title: The canal belt after dark
activities.description: Seventeenth-century merchant wealth laid out in three concentric rings, now a UNESCO site and still the actual experience of the city. Brouwersgracht, Egelantiersgracht, Bloemgracht. Walk it once in daylight and once when the bridges are lit — the second is the one you'll remember.

activities.title: Rijksmuseum
activities.description: The Night Watch, Vermeer's Milkmaid, and the Gallery of Honour running the length of the building. Two hours minimum, and the building is half the point.

activities.title: Van Gogh Museum
activities.description: The largest collection of his work anywhere, hung chronologically so you watch the style arrive in real time. Sunflowers, Almond Blossom, the last Auvers canvases.

activities.title: Anne Frank House
activities.description: The annex behind the bookcase, kept deliberately unfurnished at Otto Frank's request. About 90 minutes, and it will flatten you. The hardest ticket in Europe — see the booking board.

activities.title: A bike, and the whole city
activities.description: Renting a bike is itself a top-ten Amsterdam activity. Vondelpark loop, then south along the Amstel, then back through the Nine Streets.

activities.title: Evening canal cruise
activities.description: Worth it specifically after dark. Take a small open boat with a skipper who talks, never a glass-roofed barge.

activities.title: De Pijp & Albert Cuyp Market
activities.description: Stroopwafels pressed while you wait, herring if you're brave, and the best neighbourhood dinner radius in the city after the stalls pack up.

activities.title: Amsterdam Noord & NDSM
activities.description: Free ferry from behind Centraal, then a former shipyard covered wall to wall in street art. Eye Filmmuseum and the A'DAM Lookout swing on the way.

activities.title: The Nine Streets
activities.description: Nine cross-streets linking the main canals, and the best browsing and coffee grid in the Netherlands.

activities.title: Begijnhof
activities.description: A silent fourteenth-century courtyard behind an unmarked door off a shopping street. Fifteen minutes, free, and almost nobody finds it.

activities.title: Museumplein
activities.description: The lawn between the Rijks, the Van Gogh and the Concertgebouw. Where the city sits down.

activities.title: Rembrandt House Museum
activities.description: His actual studio, reconstructed down to the pigments on the shelf.

activities.title: Foodhallen
activities.description: Indoor food hall in a converted Oud-West tram depot. Good rainy evening.

activities.title: De Wallen
activities.description: Smaller and sadder than the reputation. Walk through early evening, don't linger, don't photograph anyone.

activities.title: Zaanse Schans
activities.description: Working windmills, 20 minutes by train. Touristy, photogenic, half a day.

activities.title: Haarlem or Utrecht
activities.description: Fifteen and twenty-five minutes respectively, and both prettier per square metre than Amsterdam.

activities.title: Heineken Experience
activities.description: A €25 corporate brand tour. Drink somewhere with a view instead.

activities.title: The Reichstag dome
activities.description: Foster's glass spiral sits directly above the parliamentary chamber, so the public physically walks over its own government. A mirrored funnel throws daylight down into the room below and an audio guide tracks the skyline as you climb. Free — but you must register online first, and there is no walk-up.

activities.title: Brandenburg Gate & Tiergarten
activities.description: Ten minutes at the gate, then walk west into the park. Best at first light, or after the dome at dusk.

activities.title: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
activities.description: 2,711 concrete stelae on deliberately uneven ground. Walk into the middle and the city vanishes. The Information Centre underneath is the part people skip and shouldn't.

activities.title: Berlin Wall Memorial, Bernauer Straße
activities.description: The real thing — a preserved stretch of death strip, an original watchtower, and a documentation centre with a viewing platform. This is the site that actually explains the Wall.

activities.title: Topography of Terror
activities.description: Built over the excavated cellars of the Gestapo and SS headquarters, with an outdoor exhibition running along a surviving section of Wall. Free, unflinching, and the best history exhibition in Berlin.

activities.title: Neues Museum
activities.description: Nefertiti, and Chipperfield's reconstruction that leaves the war damage deliberately visible. With the Pergamon shut, this is Museum Island's anchor.

activities.title: East Side Gallery
activities.description: 1.3 km of painted Wall along the Spree, ending at the Oberbaum Bridge and the whole of Friedrichshain.

activities.title: Museum Island
activities.description: Alte Nationalgalerie for German Romanticism, Altes Museum for antiquity, Bode for sculpture in near-empty rooms. Buy the combined day ticket.

activities.title: Gemäldegalerie
activities.description: Vermeer, Bruegel, Caravaggio, Raphael — one of Europe's great old-master collections and chronically under-visited. The best answer to the Pergamon being closed.

activities.title: Kreuzberg & Neukölln
activities.description: Turkish market on the Maybachufer canal Tuesdays and Fridays, Görlitzer Park, natural wine, and the best döner arguments on the continent.

activities.title: Tempelhofer Feld
activities.description: A decommissioned Nazi-era airport turned public park, where you cycle down the runways past kite-surfers and allotments. There is nothing else like it in any city.

activities.title: Potsdam & Sanssouci
activities.description: Frederick the Great's rococo retreat 40 minutes out on the S-Bahn — palace, vine terraces, the Dutch Quarter, and Cecilienhof where the Potsdam Conference was held.

activities.title: A night out
activities.description: Berghain — Sunday morning is the real window and rejection is normal. Otherwise Sisyphos, Renate, Watergate, or Clärchens Ballhaus for something entirely unlike the others.

activities.title: Fernsehturm
activities.description: Highest view in the EU. Book the fast-track slot or lose an hour of your life.

activities.title: Berlin Cathedral & Lustgarten
activities.description: The dome climb gives you Museum Island from above.

activities.title: Sachsenhausen Memorial
activities.description: Concentration camp memorial 45 minutes north. Free, heavy, better with a guide.

activities.title: Mauerpark flea market
activities.description: Sunday only, and your Berlin days are Monday to Wednesday. Listed so you know what you're missing.

activities.title: Checkpoint Charlie
activities.description: Costumed actors, a replica hut and a McDonald's. Three minutes. Bernauer Straße is the real thing.

activities.title: Oktoberfest at the Theresienwiese
activities.description: Sixteen days, fourteen large tents, roughly seven million people. Tables are free to enter but functionally require a reservation after about 15:00 and on weekends — walk in before noon on a weekday and you'll get a bench. Beer is served by the Maß, a full litre, at around €15. The Hofbräu tent is the international party, Augustiner is the one Müncheners pick, Schottenhamel is where the first keg gets tapped.
activities.details: 19 Sep – 4 Oct · reserve tables months ahead

activities.title: Marienplatz and the Glockenspiel
activities.description: The neo-Gothic Neues Rathaus, its carillon performing at 11:00 and 12:00, and the tower lift for the view. Climb Alter Peter opposite instead — it's cheaper and it looks at the Rathaus rather than out from it.

activities.title: Viktualienmarkt
activities.description: A permanent open-air food market since 1807, with a beer garden in the middle that rotates between the six Munich breweries. Weisswurst before noon, as tradition insists.

activities.title: Englischer Garten
activities.description: Larger than Central Park, with a Chinese pagoda beer garden, nude sunbathing that nobody remarks on, and a standing river wave at the southern tip.

activities.title: Surfers on the Eisbach
activities.description: A permanent standing wave under a bridge in the middle of a city park, surfed continuously since the 1970s. Ten minutes of watching is enough and you won't forget it.

activities.title: Hofbräuhaus
activities.description: Enormous, loud, brass band, and full of people who have travelled a long way to be there. Go once, briefly, and eat somewhere else.

activities.title: Munich Residenz
activities.description: The Wittelsbach palace — 130 rooms, and the barrel-vaulted Antiquarium is the largest Renaissance hall north of the Alps.

activities.title: Neuschwanstein
activities.description: Ludwig II's fantasy castle, two hours south by train and bus. A very long day for a twenty-minute timed tour, but it is the castle Disney copied.

activities.title: Dachau Memorial
activities.description: The first Nazi concentration camp, 30 minutes north on the S-Bahn. Free, unflinching, and the model on which the others were built. Half a day, and you will not want to do anything else afterwards.

activities.title: BMW Welt & Museum
activities.description: Free delivery hall and showroom next to a paid museum, under the four-cylinder tower. Genuinely good if you're already driving to the Nürburgring.

activities.title: Nymphenburg Palace
activities.description: Baroque summer palace with a canal down the middle and a park you could lose an afternoon in.

activities.title: Asamkirche
activities.description: A tiny late-Baroque church two brothers built next to their own house, with every surface covered. Two minutes, free, astonishing.

activities.title: Olympiapark
activities.description: The 1972 site — tent roof, tower, and the lake. Also where BMW Welt is.

activities.title: Deutsches Museum
activities.description: The world's largest science and technology museum. A full day if you let it, and partly under renovation.

activities.title: A lap of the Nordschleife
activities.description: 20.8 km, roughly 150 corners, 300 metres of elevation change, and during Touristenfahrten it is legally a one-way public toll road — so ordinary road rules apply, overtaking is left-only, and there is no official timing. €30 Monday to Thursday, €35 Friday to Sunday and holidays. Note that 3 October is German Unity Day, so holiday pricing and holiday crowds.

activities.title: Rent a car built for it — not your rental
activities.description: This matters more than anything else here. Sixt, Hertz and Europcar all explicitly prohibit the Nordschleife and your insurance will not cover it; hitting the Armco is a five-figure bill plus track closure charges. RSRNurburg, Rent4Ring and Apex Nürburg rent track-prepared cars with Nordschleife-valid insurance included, roughly €250–700 for the day.

activities.title: An instructor for your first laps
activities.description: 150 corners, most of them blind, many with no run-off. Every Ring rental company sells instructor time and it is the difference between a good day and a very expensive one. Alternatively buy a Ring Taxi hot lap in a GT3 first and just watch the lines.

activities.title: The Grand Prix circuit
activities.description: The modern F1-spec track next door, open for tourist sessions in 15-minute blocks. Far more forgiving than the Nordschleife and a sensible warm-up.

activities.title: Adenau
activities.description: The half-timbered town in the valley the track loops around. Pit stop food, cheap beds, and the Ring's unofficial paddock.

activities.title: The Eifel back roads
activities.description: The B258 and the roads around Nürburg and the Hohe Acht are, quietly, as good as the track and free. Volcanic hills, no traffic, endless corners.

activities.title: Nürburg Castle
activities.description: The 12th-century hilltop ruin the whole circuit is named after, right in the middle of the loop. Ten minutes and the best overview of the place.

activities.title: Watch from Brünnchen
activities.description: The public spectator banks at Brünnchen and Pflanzgarten cost nothing and are where you actually see how fast people are going.

activities.title: Starlight Festival at the Pyramids
activities.description: EXIT and P+US, first edition, five stages against the Giza plateau. Welcome party on the 8th across Cairo venues, the two main nights on the 9th and 10th beside the pyramids, farewell on the 11th. Charlotte de Witte, Adriatique, Michael Bibi, Pete Tong, Vintage Culture, Enrico Sangiuliano, WhoMadeWho.

activities.title: The Giza plateau
activities.description: Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, plus the queens' pyramids and the causeway. Enter at 08:00 through the main gate before the heat and the coaches. Going inside the Great Pyramid is a hot, stooped scramble up a wooden ramp — worth it once, and only once.

activities.title: The Great Sphinx
activities.description: Smaller than you expect and stranger than you expect. The Sphinx enclosure viewing area is included with the plateau ticket; go after the pyramids, before 10:00.

activities.title: Grand Egyptian Museum
activities.description: Twenty years and a billion dollars, opened November 2025, aligned on the axis of the Great Pyramid two kilometres away. All 5,398 objects from Tutankhamun's tomb shown together for the first time since 1922, plus the Ramesses II colossus and Khufu's solar boat. Three hours minimum.

activities.title: Islamic Cairo & Al-Muizz Street
activities.description: A kilometre of Fatimid, Ayyubid and Mamluk architecture, pedestrianised and lit at night. The densest concentration of medieval Islamic monuments anywhere in the world.

activities.title: Khan el-Khalili
activities.description: A souk since the fourteenth century. Coffee at El Fishawy, which has reportedly not closed since 1797. Haggle, expect to be quoted triple, enjoy it.

activities.title: Saqqara & the Step Pyramid
activities.description: Djoser's step pyramid is the oldest large stone building on earth and predates Giza by a century. Quieter, older, and for many people the better site.

activities.title: Mosque of Muhammad Ali & the Citadel
activities.description: Ottoman alabaster on the hill above the city, with the best panorama in Cairo when the haze allows.

activities.title: Mosque of Ibn Tulun
activities.description: 876 AD, mud brick and a spiral minaret, and almost always empty. The most atmospheric building in Cairo.

activities.title: Sultan Hassan & Al-Rifa'i
activities.description: Two enormous mosques facing each other across a lane. Mamluk architecture at the scale of a cathedral.

activities.title: Coptic Cairo
activities.description: The Hanging Church, Ben Ezra Synagogue and St Sergius, all inside the walls of a Roman fortress. Compact, and a completely different Cairo.

activities.title: Dahshur
activities.description: The Bent Pyramid and the Red Pyramid — Sneferu's two attempts at getting the angle right. Almost no one goes. Pair with Saqqara.

activities.title: Egyptian Museum, Tahrir
activities.description: The 1902 original. Most of the Tutankhamun material has moved to the GEM, but the Narmer Palette, the Tanis gold and the wooden-crate-and-dust atmosphere remain.

activities.title: Felucca on the Nile at sunset
activities.description: An hour under sail from the Zamalek or Garden City banks. Cheap, quiet, and the best way to see the city stop moving.

activities.title: Al-Azhar Mosque & Park
activities.description: The mosque founded in 970 AD, and a park built on a thousand years of rubbish with the best sunset view of the old city.

activities.title: Zamalek
activities.description: The island district — galleries, bookshops, and where you'll eat best.

activities.title: Cairo Tower
activities.description: 1961 lotus-shaped tower on Gezira Island. Go at dusk.

activities.title: Memphis & Mit Rahina
activities.description: The old capital, now a small open-air museum with a colossal recumbent Ramesses II. Usually bundled with Saqqara.

activities.title: Sound and light at the Sphinx
activities.description: Deeply dated, faintly magnificent. Your call.

oi.title: Mercedes-Benz Museum
oi.description: The strongest standalone automotive museum detour for your trip: early motoring, design, engineering and motorsport. Give it a proper morning.

oi.status: Hours / free Welt entry checked Sep 5
oi.access: Central Munich → Olympiazentrum by U-Bahn + walk ~25–35min each way. Paid museum tariff: check ticket shop.

oi.title: Porsche Museum
oi.description: Racing and sports-car focus. An excellent partner to Mercedes if you can give Stuttgart a full day.
oi.details: Tue–Sun 09:00–18:00 · allow 2–3h · check current ticket price

oi.title: Classic Remise Berlin
oi.description: Classic and exotic cars in a restored tram depot; workshops, dealers and glass storage bays. A strong short stop within your Berlin stay.

oi.access: Mitte → Moabit ~25–40min each way by public transport.

oi.title: Autoworld Brussels

oi.details: Weekdays 10:00–17:00; weekends to 18:00 · allow 1½–2½h · check exhibition tariff
oi.access: Grand Place → museum ~25–35min by metro + walk.

oi.title: Motorworld Munich

oi.access: Central Munich → Freimann ~35–50min each way; allow extra time between this and BMW.

oi.title: Klassikstadt Frankfurt
oi.description: Classic-car workshops, showrooms and collectors’ vehicles. Only add it if arrival energy and pickup timing allow.

oi.title: Audi Forum · museum mobile

oi.title: Autostadt + ZeitHaus

oi.status: Hours checked Sep 5 · rail connection unverified

si.title: Main Market Square, Cloth Hall & St Mary’s
si.description: Start with the historic centre and Royal Route; return to the square in the evening.

si.title: Wawel Castle & Cathedral
si.description: Royal history, architecture and views above the Vistula. Choose specific interiors instead of trying every ticketed section.

si.title: Kazimierz & Jewish heritage
si.description: Synagogues, courtyards, cafés and the history of Kraków’s Jewish community. Combine with a guided heritage walk.

si.title: Oskar Schindler’s Enamel Factory
si.description: The main exhibition covers Kraków under Nazi occupation. Book a timed slot and combine it with nearby Podgórze.

si.title: Rynek Underground
si.description: Archaeology below the market square; a useful choice for a rainy afternoon.

si.title: Wieliczka Salt Mine
si.description: A substantial underground visit with a guided route. Choose this or Auschwitz for a day-trip block if staying only three nights.

si.title: Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial
si.description: Give the memorial an unhurried day with advance reservations and transport planning. Avoid stacking entertainment immediately afterward.
si.details: Full day including transfers · reserve official entry / guide

si.title: Podgórze & Ghetto Heroes Square
si.description: A reflective walk around the former ghetto district and memorial square.

si.title: Planty Park & Vistula walk
si.description: A low-effort arrival-day loop outside the old city walls, then riverside toward Wawel.

si.title: Czartoryski Museum
si.description: A focused art stop, especially for Leonardo’s Lady with an Ermine.

si.title: Pierogi, cafés & Kazimierz dinner
si.description: Look for potato-and-cheese, mushroom or other vegetarian pierogi; ask for no bacon, lard or pork garnish.
si.details: Meal budget varies · ingredients must be confirmed

si.title: Market Square, Town Hall & the Old Town
si.description: Start with Rynek, the Gothic Town Hall, colourful merchant houses and the compact lanes immediately around the square.

si.title: Ostrów Tumski & Cathedral Island
si.description: Walk the bridges to Wrocław’s oldest quarter around dusk, when the island is at its most atmospheric.

si.title: Racławice Panorama
si.description: A singular 19th-century panoramic painting presented in its purpose-built rotunda; reserve a timed entry.
si.details: Allow 1–1½h · check time slot and ticket

si.title: Museum of the History of Wrocław
si.description: Useful context for a city shaped by German, Polish, Jewish, Habsburg and postwar histories.

si.title: Centennial Hall & Szczytnicki Park
si.description: UNESCO-listed concrete landmark with park, Japanese Garden and the zoo complex nearby.
si.details: Half day with park / garden · check individual admissions

si.title: University Quarter & Oder river walk
si.description: Walk from the baroque University through the university quarter and across the river islands.

si.title: Wrocław dinner in the Four Temples District
si.description: Good compact area for cafés and restaurants near the Old Town. Ask explicitly about broth, bacon, lard and seafood ingredients.
si.details: Meal budget varies · ingredients must be confirmed

si.title: Hydropolis
si.description: A highly visual museum about water, engineering and the city’s relationship with the Oder; a strong indoor alternative.

si.title: Wrocław Zoo & Afrykarium
si.description: The zoo’s signature oceanarium-style Africa complex is one of the city’s biggest attractions; prioritize it only if wildlife exhibits interest you.

si.title: Japanese Garden
si.description: A calm landscaped garden beside Centennial Hall that fits naturally into the same east-side half day.

si.title: Kolejkowo
si.description: A detailed miniature world of Lower Silesia and Wrocław—playful, visually rich and a good rain-day option.

si.title: Neon Side Gallery
si.description: A courtyard of restored Polish neon signs in the Four Temples District; best as a short evening stop near dinner.

si.title: Wrocław Market Hall
si.description: Historic brick market hall for produce, flowers and a quick local-food browse between Old Town and Cathedral Island.

si.title: National Museum in Wrocław
si.description: Polish and Silesian art in a landmark ivy-covered building; pair it with the Panorama rather than crossing town twice.

si.title: Oder islands & river cruise
si.description: See the city from its bridges and islands, or take a seasonal cruise when weather and schedules cooperate.

si.title: Collegium Maius
si.description: The Jagiellonian University’s historic courtyard and museum add science, scholarship and architecture just off the Main Square.

si.title: MOCAK Museum of Contemporary Art
si.description: Contemporary Polish and international art beside Schindler’s Factory; the two make an efficient Podgórze museum block.

si.title: Nowa Huta architecture & history
si.description: Explore the planned socialist-realist district for a completely different side of Kraków; best with a focused guided tour.
si.details: Half day with tram · tour optional

si.title: Kościuszko Mound
si.description: Panoramic city and landscape views from a historic memorial mound west of the centre.

si.title: Stained Glass Museum & workshop
si.description: A compact working-studio visit that reveals how Kraków’s Art Nouveau stained glass is designed and made.

si.title: Krakus Mound & Liban quarry viewpoint
si.description: A free sunset option with broad city views; combine with Podgórze only if you still have walking energy.

si.title: National Museum in Kraków
si.description: The main building is a flexible art-and-design alternative when weather is poor or temporary exhibitions appeal.

si.title: Tyniec Abbey
si.description: A peaceful Benedictine abbey above the Vistula, best treated as a slow half-day escape rather than squeezed between Old Town sights.

si.title: Long Market & the Motława waterfront
si.description: Walk Długi Targ, Neptune’s Fountain, the waterfront and Granary Island; return after sunset.

si.title: European Solidarity Centre
si.description: Labour organising, political opposition and democratic transition. A particularly strong match for your politics and economics interests.

si.title: Museum of the Second World War
si.description: A substantial museum covering the war and civilian experience. Allocate a separate half-day if you also visit ECS.

si.title: Mariacka Street & St Mary’s Church
si.description: Amber shops and atmospheric façades; climb the church tower only if you want the stairs.

si.title: Historic shipyard & Gate No. 2
si.description: Connect the Solidarity story with the former shipyard district and workers’ monument.

si.title: Sopot beach & pier
si.description: A lighter coastal half-day between museum visits. Use local rail and walk down to the sea.
si.details: ~25–35min train each way; allow half day

si.title: Malbork Castle
si.description: Large brick castle complex; worthwhile only if you have a full spare day for the journey and interiors.

si.title: Westerplatte
si.description: A historic peninsula associated with the opening of World War II in Poland. Check bus or seasonal boat service.

si.title: Oliwa Park & Cathedral
si.description: Quieter gardens and architecture northwest of the centre; organ recital availability depends on the day.

si.title: Amber Museum
si.description: A compact material-culture alternative if two large history museums would be too much.

si.title: Gravensteen · Castle of the Counts
si.description: Medieval castle in the city centre, with an included audio guide.

si.title: St Bavo’s Cathedral & Ghent Altarpiece
si.description: Build your Ghent day around Van Eyck’s altarpiece, then walk the historic centre.

si.title: Graslei, Korenlei & St Michael’s Bridge
si.description: The waterfront and bridge give you the city’s best compact walking circuit. Stay for the evening lighting if possible.

si.title: Patershol & Vrijdagmarkt
si.description: Old lanes and a good dinner area to round out a day trip.

si.title: Römerberg, New Old Town & cathedral
si.description: The most compact Frankfurt arrival-day walk if you sleep in the city on September 22.

si.title: Main river & Eiserner Steg
si.description: A short skyline walk that is easy to fit around car collection.

si.title: Städel Museum
si.description: A substantial art museum on the museum embankment. Only add it if you have a genuine half-day.

si.title: Main Tower observation deck
si.description: Skyline view; check weather and access before allocating the visit.

si.title: ECB Visitor Centre
si.description: Relevant to your economics interests, but access requires advance planning rather than an arrival-day walk-in assumption.

si.title: Cologne Cathedral & Rhine
si.description: A useful stop only if you route through Cologne. Allow for luggage and station transfers.

si.title: Deutsches Museum Verkehrszentrum
si.description: A transport-focused alternative covering road and rail vehicles, near Theresienwiese.

si.title: Mercedes-Benz Museum - Stuttgart day trip
si.description: A high-value automotive detour if you are willing to protect a full day for Stuttgart. Pair it with the Porsche Museum only if you convert it into an overnight, not a rushed Munich return.
si.details: Full day from Munich by ICE plus local transit · museum 3-4h · reserve transport
si.pairing: Use this instead of a second Munich museum day; do not pair with Neuschwanstein.

si.title: Munich Documentation Centre for the History of National Socialism
si.description: A valuable historical complement to the city’s royal palaces and automotive collections.

si.title: House of European History
si.description: A strong complement to the Parlamentarium, focusing on European history beyond individual national narratives.
